note: quince#103: step() wrote the observation plus {observed: true} and carried forward only `.issues`, so EVERY write dropped `.watch`. The watcher survived because tick()'s watcher branch rewrites its own record immediately after step(); a HAND-RUN tick has no such branch, so it erased the record of a watcher it does not own. The comment on tick()'s write claimed a hand tick 'can never make a dead watcher look alive' — true, and the direction that does not matter. The broken mirror is worse: a live watcher read as dead, so `watch_preflight`'s live-refusal does not fire and the next arm puts a SECOND watcher on one state file — quince#50's race, reached through the guard rather than around it. quince#100's ruling then put a foreground tick immediately before every arm, turning a latent bug into the standard turn shape. Both step() write paths are covered here because the bug was in both: tick 0 takes the first-observation path (initial has no `observed`), tick 1 takes the main path. NOTE this fixture asserts STATE, not events — the events were correct throughout, which is why all 38 existing fixtures passed against the defect. That assertion did not exist before this fixture (see compare_state).
